https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 美国司法部周四提起诉讼，试图预先阻止阿拉斯加州认证其美国参议院选举结果，以防共和党现任候选人以微弱差距败选。司法部称，选票上有两名名字几乎相同的共和党人，可能令选民混淆。美国参议院的控制权可能取决于阿拉斯加州，现任共和党参议员丹·S.的选举结果尚未确定。选举法专家表示，美国司法部的诉讼毫无依据，所请求的救济也不符合联邦法律的规定。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: The US Justice Department on Thursday sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses by a narrow margin, saying voters could be confused because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names. The lawsuit signals the willingness of President Donald Trump's administration to contest the results of the November 3 midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress. Trump's administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including both Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola. The Justice Department's lawsuit, filed in federal court in Anchorage, takes issue with the presence of a third contender in the race, another Republican named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, alleging he is running "with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him." The lawsuit asks a federal judge to block the certification of an outcome "that may be impacted by voter confusion," so that there can be "an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan." Trump told reporters on Friday that he supported the lawsuit, saying "I'm the one that said do it." Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are preparing for potential federal interference in November’s elections, including legal challenges and disputes over voting that could disrupt certification of the results. Trump has a long history of challenging election outcomes and encouraging supporters to contest results he views as unfavorable. Election law experts said the Justice Department's lawsuit has no merit and seeks relief not allowed under federal law. The unelected Sullivan, a former US Forest Service worker and elementary school teacher, filed to run as a candidate on May 29 seeking to unseat Senator Dan S. Sullivan and "put Alaska first," according to his campaign website, which advertised "Dan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for US Senate Seat." Dan J. Sullivan has denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan. The Alaska Supreme Court in June permitted the unelected Sullivan to appear on the ballot. He will appear without a party designation next to his name, while the senator will be listed as the Republican incumbent. Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low, hit by rising diesel and gasoline prices and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters. Public opinion polls suggest Republicans may lose control of one or both houses of Congress, which would likely limit Trump's ability to enact his policies in the final two years of his presidency
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 美国司法部起诉阻止民主党人可能当选阿拉斯加州联邦参议员
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 美国司法部周四提起诉讼，试图预先阻止阿拉斯加州认证美国参议院选举结果，以防共和党现任候选人在以微弱差距落败时该州仍认证结果。司法部称，选票上有两名名字几乎相同的共和党人，可能令选民混淆。这起诉讼表明，总统唐纳德·特朗普政府愿意就决定美国国会控制权的11月3日中期选举结果提出异议。特朗普政府对选举监督采取了日益强硬的做法，敦促各州提供选民登记数据，并主张需要采取更严格的措施，以确保公众对投票结果的信心。包括民主党人士和部分共和党选举官员在内的批评者认为，这些举措是联邦政府越权。美国参议院的控制权可能取决于阿拉斯加州。现任共和党参议员丹·S·沙利文正与民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉展开势均力敌的竞选。司法部在安克雷奇联邦法院提起的诉讼针对的是该州出现了第三名竞选人——另一名共和党人丹·J·沙利文 Jr，指控他参选的“意图是误导参议员沙利文的支持者把票投给他”。诉讼要求联邦法官阻止认证可能“因选民混淆而受到影响”的选举结果，以便“展开调查，确定投给丹尼尔·J·沙利文 Jr的选票是否本应投给参议员沙利文”。特朗普周五告诉记者，他支持这起诉讼，并表示：“就是我要求这么做的。”全国各地的选举官员已告知路透社，他们正为11月选举中可能出现的联邦干预做准备，其中包括法律挑战和投票争议，这些情况可能扰乱选举结果的认证。特朗普长期以来质疑选举结果，并鼓励支持者对他认为不利的结果提出异议。选举法专家表示，司法部的诉讼毫无依据，所请求的救济措施不为联邦法律所允许。尚未当选的沙利文曾是美国林务局工作人员和小学教师。他于5月29日登记参选，欲击败参议员丹·S·沙利文，并按照其竞选网站的说法，把“阿拉斯加放在首位”；该网站登有“丹·沙利文挑战丹·沙利文，角逐美国参议院席位”。丹·J·沙利文 Jr在接受美国新闻机构采访时否认，自己的目的是制造混淆或分流投给丹·S·沙利文的选票。阿拉斯加州最高法院6月允许尚未当选的沙利文出现在选票上。他的姓名旁不会标注党派，而现任参议员将被列为共和党现任议员。随着柴油和汽油价格上涨以及中东冲突不受选民欢迎，特朗普的支持率已降至历史低点。民意调查显示，共和党可能失去对国会两院中一院或两院的控制权，这大概会限制特朗普在任期最后两年推行其政策的能力

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Army has activated an air defense battalion in Guam to bolster the island's defenses against regional missile threats, including those posed by North Korea and China, a U.S. military news outlet reported Friday. The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, held an activation ceremony on Oct. 16 at Andersen Air Force Base in Guam and will assume the air defense responsibilities previously carried out by Task Force Talon, according to USNI News. Task Force Talon began its rotational mission in 2013 to counter potential North Korean ballistic missile threats, but its responsibilities have since expanded amid China's growing missile capabilities, the report said. The newly activated battalion is expected to operate Patriot, Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) and Intermediate Fires Protection Capability (IFPC) systems as part of a layered defense network against ballistic and cruise missiles, aircraft and drones. "Guam's strategic location makes it an important part of U.S. military operations throughout the region by supporting joint force operations while making air and missile defense a critical part of protecting the forces and infrastructure needed to support those missions," the Army told USNI News. According to the Army, the transition from a rotational task force to a battalion reflects the Pentagon's commitment to establishing permanent air defense capabilities in the Indo-Pacific. Guam, a strategically important U.S. territory in the western Pacific, currently relies on THAAD launchers and U.S. Navy Aegis-equipped warships on an as-needed basis for air and missile defense, according to the report
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 报道称，面对朝鲜和中国导弹威胁，美陆军在关岛启动防空营
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 华盛顿——美国一家军事新闻网站周五报道称，美国陆军已在关岛启动一个防空营，以加强该岛应对区域性导弹威胁的防御能力，其中包括朝鲜和中国带来的威胁。据USNI News报道，第43防空炮兵团第3营于10月16日在关岛安德森空军基地举行启动仪式，并将接管此前由“利爪特遣队”承担的防空任务。报道称，“利爪特遣队”于2013年开始轮换部署任务，旨在应对潜在的朝鲜弹道导弹威胁，但随着中国导弹能力不断增强，其职责此后有所扩大。新启动的营预计将操作“爱国者”系统、“终端高空区域防御”（THAAD）系统以及“中间火力防护能力”（IFPC）系统，作为分层防御网络的一部分，应对弹道导弹和巡航导弹、飞机及无人机。陆军向USNI News表示：“关岛具有重要的战略位置，是美国在整个地区开展军事行动的重要组成部分；它通过支援联合部队行动，使防空和反导成为保护相关兵力及基础设施的关键环节，而这些都是支援上述任务所必需的。”据陆军称，从轮换特遣队转为建制营，反映出五角大楼致力于在印太地区建立永久性防空能力。报道称，关岛是西太平洋具有重要战略意义的美国领地，目前主要根据需要依靠THAAD发射器和装备美国海军“宙斯盾”系统的军舰执行防空和反导任务

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title: Lee showed how he uses AI. Trump isn't telling
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: Across the Pacific, U.S. President Donald Trump has taken a different approach: He acknowledges using artificial intelligence (AI) but won't say exactly how. Trump is hardly shy about AI-generated content. Pressed on how he uses the technology, Trump replied, "Well, I don't want to tell you that." The exchange illustrates a contrast with Lee, who publicly shared a Gemini-generated response to support his position on whether the heads of investigative agencies should attend Cabinet meetings.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 在太平洋彼岸，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普采取了不同的做法：他承认使用人工智能（AI），但拒绝说明具体如何使用。特朗普对人工智能生成的内容毫不避讳。当被追问如何使用这项技术时，特朗普回答：“嗯，我不想告诉你们。”这段对话凸显了他与Lee之间的反差。Lee曾公开分享一段由Gemini生成的回应，以支持他关于调查机构负责人是否应出席内阁会议的立场。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: SEATTLE — President Lee Jae Myung has come under fire for publicly sharing how he used Google's Gemini to support his position in a political dispute. Across the Pacific, U.S. President Donald Trump has taken a different approach: He acknowledges using artificial intelligence (AI) but won't say exactly how. Trump is hardly shy about AI-generated content. His social media accounts have featured a string of fabricated images and videos, including portrayals of himself as a pope and a king, as well as AI-generated content mocking political opponents. But when reporters asked Trump about his personal use of AI aboard Air Force One last month, he offered little insight. Pressed on how he uses the technology, Trump replied, "Well, I don't want to tell you that." The exchange illustrates a contrast with Lee, who publicly shared a Gemini-generated response to support his position on whether the heads of investigative agencies should attend Cabinet meetings. Lee's disclosure sparked criticism from opposition politicians, who questioned his reliance on a chatbot to address legal and constitutional matters. The presidential office maintained that Lee had used Gemini to verify legal facts, not to make government decisions. While Trump's public embrace of AI-generated political imagery is well documented, his remarks offered no indication of whether he personally consults chatbots on policy or legal questions. Other American politicians, however, have been more forthcoming about their use of the technology. Sen. Tommy Tuberville, a Republican from Alabama, told The Washington Post in August that he consults ChatGPT during long drives to learn about issues such as Medicare and Medicaid. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, a Florida Republican, defended her staff's use of AI after a summary accompanying a defense bill amendment inadvertently included text generated by Anthropic's Claude. The growing use of AI in American politics has raised questions about accuracy, transparency and accountability, particularly when elected officials rely on chatbot-generated information in their work. In an August analysis published by the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, researchers Danaé Metaxa and Alex Engler highlighted the growing influence of AI chatbots on political discourse and the challenges of evaluating their responses. "We see LLMs’ impact on political discourse as a critical new frontier of modern politics," they wrote, referring to large language models, the technology behind AI chatbots. The researchers also noted that AI chatbots can produce different responses even when given identical questions. The dispute surrounding Lee's use of Gemini also illustrated how different questions about the same political issue can yield conflicting AI-generated responses. Rep. Na Kyung-won of the main opposition People Power Party said she had also consulted Gemini about the issue and received a response warning that justifying the attendance of investigative agency chiefs through presidential supervisory authority could threaten their political neutrality. Na accused Lee of framing his question to obtain a favorable response

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 西雅图——李在明总统因公开分享自己如何使用谷歌Gemini支持其在一场政治争议中的立场而受到抨击。在太平洋彼岸，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普采取了不同的做法：他承认使用人工智能（AI），但不愿具体说明如何使用。特朗普对人工智能生成的内容并不避讳。他的社交媒体账号发布过一系列虚假图片和视频，其中包括把自己描绘成教皇和国王的形象，以及嘲笑政治对手的人工智能生成内容。然而，上个月，当记者询问特朗普在“空军一号”机上如何使用这项技术时，他几乎没有透露多少信息。记者追问其使用方式，特朗普回答：“嗯，我不想告诉你们。”这一交流凸显了他与李在明之间的反差。李在明公开分享了一段由Gemini生成的回复，以支持自己关于调查机构负责人是否应出席内阁会议的立场。李在明的披露引发了反对派政治人士的批评，他们质疑他依赖聊天机器人处理法律和宪法事务。总统府表示，李在明使用Gemini是为了核实法律事实，而非作出政府决策。尽管特朗普公开拥抱人工智能生成的政治图像已有多方记录，但他的言论并未表明他本人是否会就政策或法律问题咨询聊天机器人。不过，其他美国政治人士对这项技术的使用情况更加坦率。阿拉巴马州共和党参议员汤米·图伯维尔8月告诉《华盛顿邮报》，他会在长途驾车期间咨询ChatGPT，了解Medicare和Medicaid等议题。佛罗里达州共和党众议员安娜·保利娜·卢纳为工作人员使用人工智能辩护。此前，一份随国防法案修正案提交的摘要意外包含了Anthropic的Claude生成的文字。人工智能在美国政治中的日益广泛使用，引发了有关准确性、透明度和问责制的疑问，尤其是在民选官员将聊天机器人生成的信息用于工作的情况下。卡内基国际和平基金会8月发布的一项分析中，研究人员达娜埃·梅塔克萨和亚历克斯·恩格勒强调，人工智能聊天机器人对政治话语的影响日益增强，也给评估其回复带来了挑战。他们写道：“我们认为，大语言模型对政治话语的影响是现代政治的一项关键新前沿。”这里所说的大语言模型，是人工智能聊天机器人背后的技术。研究人员还指出，即使面对完全相同的问题，人工智能聊天机器人也可能给出不同回复。围绕李在明使用Gemini的争议也说明，针对同一政治议题提出不同问题，可能得到相互冲突的人工智能生成回复。执政的反对党国民力量党议员娜 Kyung-won表示，她也曾就这一问题咨询Gemini，并收到一条警告称，以总统监督权为调查机构负责人出席内阁会议作辩护，可能威胁这些负责人的政治中立性。娜指责李在明通过设计问题来获得有利回复……

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title: US Treasury proposes expanding tech investment restrictions to N. Korea
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Treasury Department has proposed expanding restrictions on American investments in sensitive technologies to include North Korea and several other countries, as Washington seeks to prevent adversaries from using U.S. capital to develop advanced military capabilities.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 华盛顿——美国财政部提议扩大对美国人投资敏感技术的限制，将朝鲜和其他多个国家纳入限制范围；华盛顿希望借此阻止对手利用美国资本发展先进军事能力。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Treasury Department has proposed expanding restrictions on American investments in sensitive technologies to include North Korea and several other countries, as Washington seeks to prevent adversaries from using U.S. capital to develop advanced military capabilities. The proposed regulations, detailed in a notice scheduled to be published in the Federal Register on Thursday, would expand the existing Outbound Investment Security Program, which currently covers China, including Hong Kong and Macau, to include North Korea, Russia, Iran and Cuba, according to the Treasury Department. The proposal seeks to implement the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, enacted in December last year as part of the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act. Under the proposal, certain investments by U.S. persons involving covered foreign entities engaged in specified sensitive technologies would be prohibited, while other transactions would be subject to notification requirements. The regulations would cover specified activities in key technology sectors, including semiconductors, microelectronics, artificial intelligence (AI), quantum information technologies, high-performance computing and supercomputing. "The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. The proposed regulations are subject to public comments through Dec. 7, with the department expected to issue final implementing rules at a later date
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 美国财政部提议将技术投资限制扩大至朝鲜
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 华盛顿——美国财政部提议扩大对美国在敏感技术领域投资的限制，将朝鲜和其他几个国家纳入其中，因为华盛顿寻求防止对手利用美国资本发展先进军事能力。根据财政部消息，将于周四在《联邦公报》公布的通知中详细说明的拟议法规，将把现有的对外投资安全计划从目前涵盖中国（包括香港和澳门）扩大到包括朝鲜、俄罗斯、伊朗和古巴。该提议旨在实施去年12月作为2026财年国防授权法一部分颁布的《全面对外投资国家安全法》。根据提议，美国人员对从事特定敏感技术的特定外国实体进行的某些投资将被禁止，而其他交易则需遵守通知要求。这些法规将涵盖关键技术领域的特定活动，包括半导体、微电子、人工智能（AI）、量子信息技术、高性能计算和超级计算。财政部长斯科特·贝森特在一份声明中表示：“拟议法规将加强现有的对外投资安全计划，防止我们的对手利用美国投资开发威胁美国国家安全的关键技术。”拟议法规将在12月7日前接受公众评论，财政部预计将在晚些时候发布最终实施规则。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy on the doorstep of midterm congressional elections centering on affordability issues, a survey showed on Friday. The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 一项周五公布的调查显示，随着中东冲突导致物价上涨，在以生活成本问题为核心的国会中期选举前夕，美国消费者信心小幅下降，接近纪录低位。密歇根大学消费者调查称，其消费者信心指数本月从9月终值48.1降至48.0。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: U.S. consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy on the doorstep of midterm congressional elections centering on affordability issues, a survey showed on Friday. The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 46.3, which had also been the index's preliminary reading for October. October's reading marked the second-lowest on record after the all-time low of 44.8 set in May, not long after the Iran war began. "Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10 percent below a year ago and 15 percent less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict." The survey results dovetail with political polling data showing voters have a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's stewardship over it. University of Michigan data broken down by political party affiliation showed the weaker sentiment was led by survey respondents self-identified as independents, who comprise a critical bloc of swing voters. Their sentiment score dropped to 42.4 — just above May's record-low 40.6 — from 47.7 in September, while scores for Democrats and Republicans improved. The survey showed a significant upswing this year among independents — and also notably Republicans — citing high prices as a drag on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents referencing inflation pressures as hurting their financial situation rose by 27 percent, while it has shot up by 52 percent among Republicans. Similar citations among Democrats, meanwhile, are up by 15 percent. Households with no or limited exposure to the stock market — until recently climbing rapidly on enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence investment boom — also have cited high prices as a drag on their finances more frequently than at the start of the year. The survey's measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the next year nudged up to 4.7 percent from 4.6 percent in September. Twelve-month inflation expectations have surged from 3.4 percent in February before the US-Israeli war with Iran started. Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years rose to 3.5 percent from 3.4 percent in September and 3.2 percent in March, just after the war's start. Hsu, in an accompanying report on inflation expectations released with the October sentiment survey, said the persistence of elevated inflation expectations in the post-COVID-19 pandemic era posed a risk for Federal Reserve policymakers' efforts to return inflation to their 2 percent target — unachieved now for more than five years. "Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu wrote. "The fact that aggregate consumer spending has been relatively resilient despite negative views of the economy provides another reason for caution. If part of consumption currently reflects precautionary spending to avoid future price hikes, disinflation may be even more difficult to achieve." Fed officials meet next week in Washington, and despite recent higher-than-expected inflation readings in the last two weeks they are broadly expected to leave their policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75 percent-4.00 percent after raising it by a quarter percentage point in September. Most Fed officials have indicated they see a need for higher rates, but key leaders also have expressed a willingness to wait for more data before their next move
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 美国消费者信心接近纪录低点，中期选举即将到来
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 美国消费者信心在10月小幅降至接近纪录低位，原因是中东冲突推高物价；在以生活成本问题为核心的国会中期选举前夕，一项周五发布的调查显示，家庭对经济的看法因物价上涨而转差。密歇根大学消费者调查称，其消费者信心指数本月从9月最终读数的48.1降至48.0。路透社调查的经济学家此前预测该指数为46.3，这同样是该指数10月的初值。10月读数创下有纪录以来第二低水平，仅高于5月创下的历史最低值44.8；当时伊朗战争开始不久。消费者调查负责人Joanne Hsu表示：“购买力继续主导消费者对经济的看法。消费者信心目前较一年前低10%，较2月低15%，而2月正值伊朗冲突爆发前夕。”调查结果与政治民调数据相互印证，后者显示选民对经济以及美国总统Donald Trump和共和党对经济的治理持负面看法。密歇根大学按党派划分的数据显示，情绪较为疲弱的是自我认定为独立人士的受访者，他们构成摇摆选民中的关键群体。其信心得分从9月的47.7降至42.4，仅略高于5月创下的纪录最低值40.6；与此同时，民主党和共和党受访者的得分均有改善。调查显示，今年独立人士的情绪明显下降，共和党人士的情绪下降也较为显著；他们将高物价列为拖累个人财务状况的因素。自1月以来，提到通胀压力损害个人财务状况的独立人士比例上升27%，共和党人士则猛增52%。与此同时，民主党人士作出类似表述的比例上升15%。未接触或较少接触股市的家庭——股市直到最近还因人工智能投资热潮而快速上涨——也越来越频繁地将高物价列为拖累个人财务状况的因素。调查显示，消费者对未来一年通胀的预期从9月的4.6%小幅升至4.7%。在美以对伊朗战争爆发前，12个月通胀预期曾为3.4%，此后已大幅上升。消费者对未来五年通胀的预期从9月的3.4%和3月的3.2%升至3.5%；3月正值战争爆发后不久。Hsu在随10月消费者信心调查一同发布的通胀预期报告中说，在新冠疫情后时代，高通胀预期持续存在，给美联储决策者将通胀恢复至2%目标的努力带来风险；这一目标至今已有5年多未能实现。Hsu写道：“消费者普遍预计通胀将加速上升，而且今年通胀预期的增长并不局限于政治光谱中的某一派别。尽管消费者对经济持负面看法，但总体消费支出仍相对有韧性，这为保持谨慎提供了另一个理由。如果目前部分消费支出是为了防范未来涨价而进行的预防性消费，那么实现通胀回落可能更加困难。”美联储官员将于下周在华盛顿会面。尽管过去两周公布的通胀数据高于预期，但市场普遍预计，在9月加息25个基点后，美联储将在下次会议上维持3.75%-4.00%的政策利率不变。多数美联储官员已表示需要提高利率，但一些关键领导人也表示，愿意在下一次调整政策前等待更多数据

Rising oil prices weighed heavily on the broader market, where three out of every four stocks within the benchmark S&P 500 index fell. Rising oil prices that weighed down much of the market helped boost energy companies.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 纽约消息——由于油价上涨带来的压力不断加大，华尔街股市周五走低。油价上涨对大盘造成显著拖累，标普500指数成分股中有四分之三下跌。油价上涨压制了大多数板块的市场表现，同时推动能源企业股价上涨。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: NEW YORK — Stocks slipped on Wall Street Friday under increasing pressure from rising oil prices. The S&P 500 fell 0.2 percent, adding to its decline from a day before. The index is on track for a second-straight week of losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 541 points, or 1 percent, as of 11:12 a.m. Eastern time. The Nasdaq composite rose 0.2 percent, bolstered by gains for several big tech stocks that also helped ease losses elsewhere. Rising oil prices weighed heavily on the broader market, where three out of every four stocks within the benchmark S&P 500 index fell. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 2.4 percent to $115.86. It has surged from less than $97 at the start of October and is now at its highest level since March. Several AI-related companies made big moves. Micron Technology jumped 3.4 percent and Microsoft rose 0.8 percent and helped ease the impact on major indexes from a broad drop for most stocks. Even a relatively small 0.3 percent gain from Nvidia went a long way to help offset losses elsewhere in the market. The tech sector's influence is also capable of quickly switching over to a heavy weight. Stocks that have benefited from the frenzy over AI have been swinging over rising worries about their path ahead. Investors are worried about whether their high prices are justified. Many of those companies have been borrowing to fund investments in AI technology and high interest rates are making those loans more expensive. The latest round of corporate earnings are being closely-watched to help get a better sense of whether those investments are paying off, or might pay off. Several influential AI-related companies report their latest financial results next week, including Google's parent, Alphabet, along with Microsoft and Amazon. Industrial companies had some of the broadest losses. Caterpillar slumped 2.3 percent and Boeing fell 1 percent. American Express slumped 3.3 percent and joined a drop for other financial companies, despite r eporting profits for its most recent quarter that beat analysts' forecasts. The company did announce its first major job cuts in roughly a decade. Rising oil prices that weighed down much of the market helped boost energy companies. Chevron rose 2.4 percent and ConocoPhillips rose 4.2 percent. European markets were lower. France’s main index fell 0.7 percent, though yields on French government bonds eased a bit. Treasury yields in the U.S. edged higher following sharp drops on Thursday. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.99 percent from 4.96 percent late Thursday. Yields have been rising globally, partly over worries about governments taking on too much debt. Inflation also remains a concern and is stubbornly well above 3 percent in the U.S. That prompted the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at its last meeting in an effort to cool inflation. Wall Street expects the central bank to hold rates steady at its meeting next week, but is leaning heavily toward another rate hike in December. Wall Street will also get several big economic updates next week, including the Fed's preferred measure of inflation. The personal consumption expenditures index, or PCE, is expected to show that inflation rose at a 3.6 percent rate in September, sharply above the Fed's 2 percent target. The U.S. war with Iran has severely cut the world's oil supply, driving energy prices higher and fueling a sharp jump in the cost of everything from gasoline to food and clothes
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 油价上涨施压，华尔街股市多数板块下跌
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh:
纽约消息——受油价上涨压力不断加大影响，华尔街股市周五走低。标普500指数下跌0.2%，跌幅在前一日基础上进一步扩大。该指数有望连续第二周录得亏损。截至美国东部时间上午11时12分，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌541点，跌幅为1%。纳斯达克综合指数上涨0.2%，几只大型科技股涨幅提振了指数，也缓解了其他股票的跌势。油价上涨给大盘带来沉重压力，标普500指数基准成分股中有四分之三下跌。布伦特原油每桶价格上涨2.4%，至115.86美元。自10月初不足97美元以来，布伦特原油价格已大幅飙升，目前处于3月以来的最高水平。

数家与人工智能有关的公司股价大幅波动。美光科技上涨3.4%，微软上涨0.8%，缓解了大多数股票下跌对主要指数造成的影响。即使英伟达仅取得0.3%的涨幅，也在很大程度上抵消了市场其他地方的损失。科技板块的影响力同样能够迅速从支撑作用转为沉重拖累。受益于人工智能热潮的股票一直随投资者对未来发展路径的担忧加剧而剧烈波动。投资者担心这些公司的高估值是否合理。其中许多公司一直借款投资人工智能技术，而高利率正在增加这些贷款的成本。市场正密切关注最新一轮企业财报，以更好地判断这些投资是否已经或将来能够获得回报。

下周，多家具有影响力的人工智能相关公司将公布最新财务业绩，其中包括谷歌母公司Alphabet、微软和亚马逊。

工业企业的跌幅在各个板块中相对较大。卡特彼勒下跌2.3%，波音下跌1%。美国运通下跌3.3%，与其他金融股一道走低，尽管该公司最近一个季度的利润超过分析师预测。该公司还宣布了约十年来首次大规模裁员。

油价上涨压低了大盘多数板块的表现，却也提振了能源企业。雪佛龙上涨2.4%，康菲石油上涨4.2%。欧洲市场走低。法国主要股指下跌0.7%，但法国国债收益率略有回落。周四大幅下挫后，美国国债收益率小幅走高。10年期美国国债收益率从周四晚间的4.96%小幅升至4.99%。全球国债收益率正在上升，部分原因是市场担忧各国政府承担过多债务。

通胀也仍是一项令人担忧的问题，在美国的同比涨幅持续明显高于3%。这促使美联储在上一次会议上提高基准利率，试图抑制通胀。华尔街预计，该央行将在下周会议上维持利率不变，但明显倾向于12月再次加息。

下周，华尔街还将迎来数项重要经济数据，其中包括美联储偏好的通胀指标。个人消费支出指数，即PCE，预计将显示9月通胀率升至3.6%，大幅高于美联储2%的目标。美国与伊朗的战争严重削减了全球石油供应，推高能源价格，并使汽油、食品和服装等各类商品成本急升

Kumaraswamy on Saturday alleged that the State government was trying to protect the accused in the sting operation case and in the case relating to the irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). Speaking to presspersons at Mavinakere in Holenarasipur, Hassan district, Mr. Kumaraswamy said that since the sting operation case surfaced, the police under Home Minister Priyank Kharge had been targeting Janata Dal (Secular) workers, including those handling the party’s social media accounts. He alleged that the Home Minister was covering up the cases by having them investigated by officers of his choice. “Former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and his son Yathindra have demanded a fair investigation into the sting operation case. However, the police are trying to protect the main accused. The government, in a way, helped him get anticipatory bail,” he alleged. He said that instead of investigating the person who admitted to conducting the sting operation, the police were going after JD(S) workers. The police had visited the workers’ homes and seized their electronic devices, the Union Minister stated. “The State government is protecting the person who conducted the sting in 2023. The Chief Minister and senior Congress leaders know why it was done. However, the government is trying to blackmail us in the name of an investigation,” he alleged. Mr. Kumaraswamy also wanted to know what had happened to the investigation into the irregularities in the KPSC examinations. He alleged that the government had moved the Supreme Court so that the probe could be conducted by officers of its choice, which he termed an attempt to cover up the case and shield the real accused. 钢铁与重型工业联邦部长H.D.库马拉斯瓦米周六表示，邦政府正试图在诱捕行动案以及卡纳塔克邦公共服务委员会（KPSC）招聘考试违规案中保护被告。库马拉斯瓦米在哈桑县霍勒纳西普尔县马维纳凯尔接受记者采访时说，自诱捕行动案曝光以来，在内政部长普里扬克·卡尔格领导下的警方一直针对人民党（世俗派）的工作人员，包括管理该党社交媒体账号的人员。他指控内政部长指定自己选择的人员调查这些案件，以掩盖真相。

他指控说：“前首席部长西达拉迈亚及其儿子亚廷德拉要求对诱捕行动案进行公正调查。然而，警方正试图保护主要被告。邦政府在某种程度上帮助他获得了预防性逮捕令。”他说，警方没有调查承认实施诱捕行动的人，反而追查JD(S)的工作人员。这名联邦部长表示，警方曾到这些工作人员家中查访，并扣押了他们的电子设备。

他指控说：“邦政府正在保护2023年实施诱捕行动的人。首席部长和国党高层都知道此举为何发生。然而，邦政府正试图打着调查的旗号勒索我们。”

库马拉斯瓦米还要求了解KPSC考试违规案的调查进展。他指控称，邦政府已向最高法院提出申请，以便由其选择的人员开展调查；他称此举是企图掩盖案件并庇护真正的被告。

Devapur Cross is a crucial junction connecting Kalaburagi with Bengaluru, and Shorapur with Vijayapura. The protesters alleged that the State government decided to stop water release from October 25 to November 2, and again during subsequent rotation schedules, to enforce the Warabandhi, despite adequate storage in the reservoir. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Naik pointed out that the district was already reeling under a severe drought, with commercial crops like cotton facing widespread damage due to a prolonged dry spell and rainfall deficit since the onset of the monsoon. However, farmers relying on irrigation from the Narayanpur Left and Right Bank Canals had cultivated paddy, groundnut, sunflower, and chilli expecting a steady water supply, he said. He criticised the decision taken during the Irrigation Consultative Committee (ICC) meeting held in Bengaluru on October 15 to enforce rotational restrictions. “The decision is unscientific. If Warabandhi is strictly implemented, standing crops will wither completely, causing irreparable losses to farmers,” Mr. Naik warned, urging the government to release water till November-end and threatening to intensify agitation if their demands were not met. The activists alleged that water from the reservoir was being released to neighboring Telangana, while local legislators who attended the ICC meeting failed to protect the interests of the district’s farming community. Pro-Kannada outfits and various local farmers’ associations extended support to the demonstration. Elaborate security arrangements were made by the police to prevent any untoward incident. Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar visited the spot and supervised security personnel throughout the demonstration. The agitators later submitted a memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister through Deputy Commissioner Rahul Pandve and Mr. Shankar. Religious leader Channamallikarjun Swami, along with local leaders Venu Madhav Naik, Suresh Sajjan, Sanganna, Bhimu Naik, Mallu Dandin, and Sharanu and others were present. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/kadu.body: The Kaduna State Government has dismissed as fabricated a viral letter alleging that Gov. Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the APC presidential campaign flag-off. The government described the purported letter as fraudulent and misleading, accusing its authors of attempting to damage the governor’s reputation for fiscal discipline and responsible governance. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, stated this in a statement on Saturday in Kaduna. Maiyaki said the letter, dated Oct. 18, 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off”, contained inconsistencies that questioned its authenticity. He said the purported letter, allegedly addressed to Sen. Abdulazeez Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, falsely claimed that N2.3 trillion was released for the campaign flag-off. The commissioner noted that Kaduna’s 2026 budget stood at N985.92 billion, making the alleged expenditure more than twice the state’s annual budget. He said the claim was financially implausible and unsupported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records. Maiyaki also identified irregularities, including the misspelling of the governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and the apparent unauthorised reproduction of his signature. “The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Gov. Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released,” he said. He described the allegation as fictitious and a deliberate attempt to mislead the public. Maiyaki said that since assuming office on May 29, 2023, Sani had prioritised fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources. He listed investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection among the administration’s priorities. The commissioner expressed concern over what he described as coordinated misinformation aimed at discrediting the governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections. He warned that fabricating official correspondence and circulating false financial claims could constitute criminal offences. “Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law,” Maiyaki said, urging critics to rely on credible evidence when questioning government expenditure. He disclosed that steps were being taken to establish the origin of the purported letter. Maiyaki also called on security and investigative agencies to examine the document and ensure that anyone found culpable faced appropriate legal action. He urged media organisations and members of the public to verify documents before circulating or publishing allegations concerning public expenditure. The commissioner reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to peace, institutional strengthening, infrastructure development, citizens’ welfare and sustainable governance. He said the government would remain focused on prudent financial management and would not be distracted by what it described as deliberate misinformation. Unlock these with Subscription North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears to have arrived on an unannounced visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong, a government source in Seoul and South Korean media said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Mr. Kim crossed via a major border bridge that only officially opened last week -- 12 years after its completion -- deepening economic ties between China and diplomatically isolated, nuclear-armed North Korea. Neither North Korea nor China disclosed Kim’s visit in advance. South Korean lawmaker Youn Kun-young said Kim was “understood” to have met Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Saturday (October 24). South Korea’s ruling Democratic Party said Mr. Youn had been briefed that Kim was likely to return home later the same day. China is North Korea’s largest trading partner and a vital source of diplomatic, economic and political support for Pyongyang, although ties have not always been smooth. The Yonhap news agency first reported Kim’s arrival, citing an unidentified South Korean government source. A separate government source told AFP that the North Korean leader appeared to have crossed into China via the recently opened New Yalu River Bridge. Lawmaker Youn said he had been briefed on Friday (October 23) about the likely visit. World leaders are preparing for November’s APEC summit in China’s Shenzhen, where it has been speculated that Kim may meet U.S. President Donald Trump. Neither the Chinese foreign ministry nor the North Korean embassy in Beijing immediately responded to AFP’s requests for comment on Saturday (October 23). South Korea’s government said it could not confirm Kim’s itinerary in China. The New Yalu River Bridge was completed in 2014 but its opening was delayed due to a lack of connecting roads and customs facilities on the North Korean side, according to South Korean news reports. Its opening came a little more than a month after North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge. By meeting Mr. Li in Dandong, Mr. Kim “may have sought to reaffirm the economic cooperation agreed during Xi Jinping’s visit to North Korea” earlier this year, and “press China to move more quickly on those commitments”, Yang Moo-jin, former president of the South’s University of North Korean Studies, told AFP . “He may also have sought Beijing’s active support and cooperation ahead of a possible summit with Trump in Shenzhen.” Hours before Yonhap’s report, North Korea’s state media said he had urged his military at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang to train to become the strongest in the world. Mr. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came the same week Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties. Seoul’s military proposed the talks on Friday (October 23) after it blamed the blast, which injured South Korean soldiers, on North Korean landmines. Pyongyang strongly rejects the claim. North Korea has not responded to the proposal and previously rejected the South’s demand for an apology over the explosion. The countries remain technically at war as their 1950-53 conflict ended in an armistice, not a peace treaty. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung -- who has repeatedly offered Pyongyang talks without preconditions -- suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze, rather than the immediate elimination, of its nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief. Critics say such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China has also appeared to move towards implicit acceptance. Mr. Kim hosted Xi Jinping in Pyongyang in June, soon after Xi held back-to-back summits in Beijing with Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin. Neither Pyongyang nor Beijing mentioned North Korean denuclearisation in their official statements -- an omission experts saw as a sign of China’s tacit consent. 据首尔一名政府消息人士和韩国媒体周六（2026年10月24日）报道，朝鲜领导人金正恩似乎已对中国边境城市丹东进行了一次未事先公布的访问。金正恩经由一座主要边境大桥过境，该桥直到上周才正式启用，而其建设早在12年前就已竣工；此举进一步深化了中国与外交孤立的核武装朝鲜之间的经济关系。朝鲜和中国均未提前披露金正恩此次访问。

韩国议员尹根镛表示，朝鲜领导人“据称”已于周六（10月24日）会见中国国务院总理李强。韩国执政党民主党称，尹根镛接到简报称，金正恩可能于当天较晚时候回国。中国是朝鲜最大的贸易伙伴，也是平壤在外交、经济和政治上的重要支持来源，尽管双方关系并非一直顺畅。

韩联社最先报道金正恩抵达的消息，并援引一名身份未公开的韩国政府消息人士。另一名政府消息人士告诉法新社，这名朝鲜领导人似乎是经由最近启用的新鸭绿江大桥进入中国。尹根镛议员说，他已于周五（10月23日）接到简报，得知金正恩很可能进行了此次访问。

各国领导人正在为11月于中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会做准备，外界猜测金正恩可能会在那里会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普。中国外交部和中国驻北京朝鲜使馆均未立即回应法新社周六（10月23日）的置评请求。韩国政府表示，无法确认金正恩在中国的行程。

据韩国新闻报道，新鸭绿江大桥于2014年竣工，但由于朝鲜一侧缺乏连接道路和海关设施，其启用被推迟。该桥启用前不久，朝鲜和俄罗斯也开通了首座公路桥。

韩国延北大学前校长杨慕真对法新社表示，金正恩在丹东会见李强总理，“可能是想重申今年早些时候习近平访问朝鲜期间达成的经济合作协议”，并“敦促中国更快履行这些承诺”。他说：“他也可能是在寻求北京的积极支持与合作，为可能在深圳与特朗普举行的峰会作准备。”

韩联社报道前数小时，朝鲜国家媒体称，金正恩在平壤举行的两天连长会议上要求军方加强训练，成为世界上最强大的军队。金正恩将他所称的“朝鲜式军事革命”提上日程之际，首尔军方提议举行会谈，以澄清非军事区（DMZ）内发生爆炸后边境局势；这场爆炸使韩朝关系进一步紧张。

首尔军方于周五（10月23日）提出会谈，称这起爆炸造成韩国士兵受伤，应归咎于朝鲜地雷。平壤强烈否认这一说法。朝鲜尚未回应这一提议，此前也拒绝了韩方就爆炸事件提出的道歉要求。两国在技术上仍处于战争状态，因为1950年至1953年的冲突最终以停战协定告终，而非和平条约。

尽管联合国制裁长期存在，朝鲜已通过法律确认其核武装国家地位，政权多次宣称其核武库是永久且不可逆转的。韩国鸽派总统李在明曾多次提出无条件与平壤对话。他于9月建议，华盛顿应以冻结朝鲜核计划、而非立即消除该计划，作为换取解除制裁的筹码。批评者称，这种做法可能默认朝鲜作为核武装国家的地位，同时让平壤在不放弃核武库的情况下获得制裁解除。分析人士称，中国似乎也正转向默认接受这一现实。

金正恩于6月在平壤接待习近平，此前习近平刚刚在北京接连与特朗普和普京举行峰会。平壤和北京在官方声明中均未提及朝鲜无核化问题，而专家认为，这种省略被视为中国默许的信号。

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription With about 10 days left for the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, talk of a Democratic wave has shifted from opinion polls to voting reality. Every major forecast now predicts the Democrats will win the House of Representatives. Statistician Nate Silver gives them a 75% chance of winning the Senate, which Republicans held strongly just a month ago. The Grand Old Party faces five main problems: a President who is a liability, weak candidates, money not swaying voters, fissures in their heartland, and a party base turning against its own. Let us begin with the President. Midterms are often a verdict on the White House. Donald Trump has made this election about himself, telling crowds to “pretend I’m on the ballot”. His approval rating is below 40%. In September, he told Republicans in tight races that he would visit “every one of those 35 places”. But he has campaigned in fewer than a third. Most stops have been in States he won easily, such as Oklahoma, Alabama, Tennessee, and Montana, which he said was his way “to thank them”. When a President rallies supporters in States that he won by huge margins two years earlier instead of margin seats, it conveys a hint of desperation. The next issue is candidate quality. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988. This year, the Republican nominee is Ken Paxton, who was impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and later acquitted by the State Senate. He was also observed partying in 2025 in Dubai with two Pakistani-American federal fugitives who were also his donors. His Democratic opponent, James Talarico, a former teacher and State legislator, was leading by two points in a Fox News poll (but the latest Fox News poll listed for October 15-19 showed a 49%-49% tie); and by three points in a University of Texas poll (September 25-October 5). The third problem is in the heartland. Kansas has sent only Republicans to this Senate seat since 1919, the longest streak for any party in U.S. history. Republican incumbent Roger Marshall is tied in the polls with Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor who started one of the country’s largest churches. In Nebraska — a State Mr. Trump won by over 20 points — Democrats have stepped aside for Dan Osborn, a former union leader running as an independent. He is about three points behind Senator Pete Ricketts. When a party spends the last two weeks defending strongholds of Kansas and Nebraska, it is on the back foot. The fourth issue is money. Elon Musk, who split from Mr. Trump last year, is now the biggest known donor in this election, having given over $276 million to Republican groups since July. Recent filings show that Mr. Musk gave $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund and a separate $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, which supports Mr. Paxton’s Senate campaign. Even so, Mr. Talarico, the Democratic candidate, is still ahead. Money can buy TV advertisements, but it cannot easily overcome a national mood shaped by high prices, an unpopular war with Iran, and immigration raids. Ohio combines these issues, making it the most revealing race. Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate backed by Mr. Trump, seemed confirmed for Governor in a State that the President has won three times. His opponent, Amy Acton, looked like an easy target. As Ohio’s highly unpopular health director during the COVID-19 pandemic, she ordered lockdowns, faced armed protesters at her home, and had Republicans try to strip her powers before she resigned in 2020. Mr. Ramaswamy and his supporters have spent about $101 million on advertisements, including $36 million of his own money, about three times what Ms. Acton has spent. Still, he was trailing her recently by about three points on average. Among independent voters, his net rating is minus 25, the lowest for a Republican candidate for Governor in Ohio this century. This week, his campaign announced plans to spend $4 million promoting an advertisement featuring Ms. Acton’s estranged mother calling her a liar, drawing criticism from Republicans, including Governor Mike DeWine and Senator Jon Husted. Much of this can be explained by the national mood, since the party’s Senate candidate in Ohio is also behind by a similar amount. But some of Mr. Ramaswamy’s problems come from within his own party. His rival in the Republican primary, Casey Putsch, posted a video of himself with a rifle inviting him to play “cowboys versus Indians”. He called Mr. Ramaswamy an “anchor baby” and said that there was “nothing remotely American” about him. Still, nearly one in five Republican primary voters picked Mr. Putsch. Far-right commentator Nick Fuentes told his followers to oppose Mr. Ramaswamy, while students at a conservative youth event questioned whether a Hindu could represent a Christian State. The anger goes back to the H-1B controversy in December 2024, when Mr. Ramaswamy said American culture undervalued excellence, which angered ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) voters. Now, the same party that once questioned who belongs in America is asking the same question about its own candidate. Ohio is an apt lesson for the Republicans. A party can get through having an unpopular President, a weak candidate, or a tough electoral map in any given year. But it is much harder when all these problems happen at once and the party’s base starts judging its own candidates by their race, background and religion. If Democrats win Texas, Kansas, Nebraska, or Ohio on November 3, it will be a wave, and the Republicans will have helped make it. Perhaps they deserve that loss. 等内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。距离美国11月3日中期选举还有约10天，关于“民主党浪潮”的讨论已从民意调查转向实际投票结果。如今，所有主要预测都认为民主党将赢得众议院。统计学家内特·银估计民主党赢得参议院的概率为75%，而共和党一个月前还稳稳控制着参议院。共和党面临五大主要问题：一位成为拖累的总统、软弱的候选人、无法左右选民的资金、其腹地内部的裂痕，以及开始反对本党的党派基础。先从总统说起。中期选举往往是对白宫执政表现的一次裁决。唐纳德·特朗普把这场选举变成了围绕自己的竞选活动，告诉支持者要“假装我也在选票上”。他的支持率低于40%。今年9月，他告诉身处胶着选区的共和党人，自己会拜访“那35个地方中的每一个”。但他实际 campaigned 的选区不到三分之一。大多数行程都安排在他轻松获胜的州，例如俄克拉何马州、阿拉巴马州、田纳西州和蒙大拿州；他说，这是为了“感谢他们”。当一位总统在两年前以巨大优势获胜的州拉票，而不是在势均力敌的选区助选时，这多少透露出他的绝望。第二个问题是候选人质量。得克萨斯州自1988年以来就没有选出过民主党参议员。今年，共和党候选人是肯·帕克斯顿，他于2023年被得克萨斯州众议院弹劾，随后又获州参议院判无罪。2025年，还有人看到他在迪拜与两名巴基斯坦裔美国联邦逃犯一起聚会，那两人也是他的捐助者。他的民主党对手詹姆斯·塔拉里科曾是一名教师和州议员，在福克斯新闻的一项民调中领先2个百分点（但福克斯新闻10月15日至19日发布的最新民调显示双方以49%对49%持平）；在得克萨斯大学9月25日至10月5日的一项民调中领先3个百分点。第三个问题出在腹地。堪萨斯州自1919年以来一直把该参议院席位交给共和党，这是美国历史上任何政党保持同一席位控制时间最长的纪录。共和党现任参议员罗杰·马歇尔在民调中与亚当·汉密尔顿持平。后者是一名卫理公会牧师，创建了美国最大的教会之一。内布拉斯加州——特朗普先生以超过20个百分点优势赢得的州——民主党没有推举候选人，转而支持以独立人士身份参选的丹·奥斯本。他是一名前工会领袖，目前落后参议员皮特·里凯茨约3个百分点。当一个政党在最后两周忙于捍卫堪萨斯州和内布拉斯加州的票仓时，它就处于被动挨打的状态。第四个问题是资金。埃隆·马斯克去年与特朗普先生分道扬镳，如今已成为本次选举中已知最大的捐助者，自7月以来向共和党团体捐赠了超过2.76亿美元。近期申报文件显示，马斯克先生向参议院领导基金捐赠了1.58亿美元，还另行向支持帕克斯顿先生参议员竞选的 Lone Star Liberty PAC 捐赠了1,000万美元。即便如此，民主党候选人塔拉里科先生仍然领先。资金可以买到电视广告，但难以轻易扭转一种全国性情绪，而这种情绪受到高物价、对伊朗战争的不满以及移民突袭的影响。俄亥俄州集这些问题于一体，因此成为最能揭示趋势的选区。特朗普先生支持的总统候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米，似乎已锁定在这个由总统三次赢得的州担任州长。他的对手艾米·阿克顿看上去是一个容易对付的目标。她在新冠疫情期间担任俄亥俄州颇不受欢迎的卫生主管时，下令实施封锁，在家中面对武装抗议者，还曾遭到共和党人试图剥夺其权力，最终她于2020年辞职。拉马斯瓦米先生及其支持者在广告上投入了约1.01亿美元，其中3,600万美元来自他本人，约为阿克顿女士支出的三倍。但截至近日，他平均仍落后她约3个百分点。在独立选民中，他的净支持率为负25，是本世纪俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人中最低的。本周，他的竞选团队宣布计划投入400万美元推广一则广告，广告中阿克顿女士关系疏远的母亲指责她撒谎，招来共和党人的批评，其中包括州长迈克·德怀恩和参议员乔恩·赫斯特德。其中很大一部分可以用全国性情绪来解释，因为该党的俄亥俄州参议员候选人也落后相近的幅度。但拉马斯瓦米先生的一些问题来自本党内部。他在共和党初选中的对手凯西·普奇发布了一段自己持步枪的视频，邀请拉马斯瓦米来玩“牛仔对印第安人”。他称拉马斯瓦米先生是“锚定婴儿”，并说他身上“没有任何 remotely American 的东西”。即便如此，近五分之一的共和党初选选民仍选择了普奇先生。极右翼评论员尼克·富恩特斯告诉追随者要反对拉马斯瓦米先生，而参加保守派青年活动的学生则质疑一名印度教徒能否代表一个基督教州。这种愤怒可以追溯到2024年12月的H-1B争议。当时，拉马斯瓦米先生说美国文化低估卓越，激怒了“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）选民。如今，这个曾质疑谁才属于美国的政党，也开始对自己的候选人提出同样的问题。俄亥俄州给共和党上了一堂合适的课。一个政党在某个特定年份即使面临不受欢迎的总统、软弱的候选人或艰难的选区版图，也有可能过关。但当所有这些问题同时出现，党派基础开始根据候选人的族裔、背景和宗教信仰评判本党候选人时，政党过关就要困难得多。如果民主党在11月3日赢得得克萨斯州、堪萨斯州、内布拉斯加州或俄亥俄州，那就会形成浪潮，而共和党将助长这一浪潮。或许他们正是咎由自取。评论必须使用英语，并且必须是完整句子。评论不得带有辱骂性或人身攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已经是《The Unlock these with Subscription Haryana Police is working with the CBI to finalise modalities for the deportation of fugitive gangster Himanshu Bhau, who has been detained by the U.S. authorities and is currently in the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), officials said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Bhau, wanted in India in multiple murder and extortion cases, was initially detained for misrepresentation of facts after Haryana Police flagged that he had fled the country using a forged surname in his passport, they said. The Special Task Force (STF) of Haryana Police is in close coordination with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's nodal agency for Interpol, to expedite his deportation from the United States, officials said. Bhau's criminal career began at the age of 17, when he allegedly attempted to murder an adversary. Although he was arrested, he escaped from a juvenile correctional facility in Hisar in 2020. Since then, he has been involved in a series of organised criminal activities, emerging as one of the most wanted criminals, they said. Investigators allege that Bhau initially fled India to Portugal using forged documents and has since operated his criminal syndicate from overseas. His gang maintains close ties with groups that are rivals of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The gang came under the spotlight in September after claiming responsibility on social media for the daylight murder of gym trainer and owner Vijay Kumar in South Delhi's Aya Nagar area. Kumar was shot dead on September 14 after being lured outside, where two motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire. Police said Kumar was the third person killed in an ongoing local family rivalry. The gang was also linked to a high-profile shootout at a Burger King outlet in Rajouri Garden in 2024, in which a 26-year-old man was killed. Unlock these with Subscription The Tamil Nadu Health Department has initiated efforts to establish a telemedicine programme based on a hub-and-spoke model, with five super speciality hubs being planned. This was one of the announcements made in the Budget earlier this year by Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson. According to the announcement, to ensure access to specialised medical care for people in remote and rural areas, the government will establish a telemedicine system based on a hub-and-spoke hospital model. Five hubs staffed by specialist doctors will be linked to 200 spokes at primary health centres and government hospitals through an online network. Over the next five years, this network will be progressively expanded to a total of 1,000 hubs and spokes. The government allocated ₹18.5 crore to establish the telemedicine network. Last week, the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, in a communication to the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) and Research, said that a proposal has been submitted to the government for the establishment of a State Hub-and-Spoke Telemedicine Programme in Tamil Nadu, with five super speciality hubs at Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital, Chennai; Government Omandurar Medical College Hospital, Chennai; Government Rajaji Hospital, Madurai Medical College, Madurai; Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital, K.A.P.V. Government Medical College, Tiruchi; and Coimbatore Medical College Hospital. It said that the space and infrastructure required for each hub was discussed during a meeting, and a type design was prepared for the super speciality hub. It went on to outline the salient features, the need for the identification of space, and the preparation of estimates through the Public Works Department (Buildings). The DME was requested to instruct the deans of the five medical college hospitals to identify existing built-up space of about 1,700 sq. ft. in the institution for their conversion into the telemedicine hub. 泰米尔纳德邦卫生部门已着手建立一套基于“中心—辐射”模式的远程医疗计划，计划设立5个超级专科中心。这是财政部长N. Marie Wilson在今年早些时候公布的预算案中宣布的举措之一。根据公布的安排，为确保偏远和农村地区民众能够获得专科医疗服务，政府将建立一套基于“中心—辐射”医院模式的远程医疗体系。5个配备专科医生的中心将通过在线网络与基层卫生中心和政府医院的200个辐射点相连。未来5年，这一网络将逐步扩展至总计1,000个中心和辐射点。政府拨款₹18.5 crore用于建立远程医疗网络。

上周，泰米尔纳德邦国家卫生使命局在发给医学教育与研究局（DME）的一份通知中表示，已向政府提交了在泰米尔纳德邦设立“邦级中心—辐射式远程医疗计划”的提案。该计划将在以下医院设立5个超级专科中心：金奈Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital；金奈Government Omandurar Medical College Hospital；马杜赖Government Rajaji Hospital、Madurai Medical College；蒂鲁吉Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital、K.A.P.V. Government Medical College；以及Coimbatore Medical College Hospital。

通知称，相关会议已讨论每个中心所需的场地和基础设施，并为超级专科中心制定了类型设计方案。通知还概述了主要事项、确定场地的必要性，以及通过公共工程部门（建筑物）编制估算的要求。DME获指示要求这5家医学院医院的院长，在各自机构内确定约1,700平方英尺的现有建成空间，用于改建远程医疗中心。计划设置8个问诊隔间和2个用于敏感问诊的私密隔间。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary: Yet when he turned his formidable historical lens on a subject that has long fascinated me, namely political Islam, I found his latest book, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval , quite unputdownable. Too often, our understanding of the North is mediated by the fragments that break into national consciousness as headlines: Boko Haram’s insurgency, the scourge of banditry, the politics of Sharia, anxieties over political Islam, and the seemingly interminable cycle of religious tension and bloodshed.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.summary_zh: 然而，当他将其非凡的历史视角转向一个长期令我着迷的议题，即政治伊斯兰主义时，我发现他的最新著作《博科圣地：当下动荡的过去》令人爱不释手。我们对北方的理解往往受到那些以头条新闻形式闯入全国意识的碎片所影响：博科圣地的叛乱、匪徒活动的祸害、伊斯兰教法的政治、对政治伊斯兰主义的焦虑，以及宗教紧张与流血冲突 seemingly 无休止的循环。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body: Having read much of Mo’s work and listened to enough of his arguments, I sometimes feel I have reached that curious point at which eating, regurgitating, and eating again begin to resemble one continuous meal. Yet when he turned his formidable historical lens on a subject that has long fascinated me, namely political Islam, I found his latest book, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval , quite unputdownable. I make this disclosure not to stake a claim to objectivity, but to establish the context in which I approach the work under review. Neither Moses nor Farooq has been a mentor to me in the conventional sense. Rather, they have been interlocutors and intellectual companions whose scholarship, arguments, and dissenting perspectives have enriched my thinking in ways that are difficult to quantify. As a Christian Southerner, I have long been struck by the ease with which those of us in the South presume to understand Northern Nigeria, while remaining only dimly acquainted with the historical currents, religious traditions, and intellectual ferment that have shaped its complex evolution. Too often, our understanding of the North is mediated by the fragments that break into national consciousness as headlines: Boko Haram’s insurgency, the scourge of banditry, the politics of Sharia, anxieties over political Islam, and the seemingly interminable cycle of religious tension and bloodshed. We encounter the North principally through the spectacle of its crises, while remaining largely estranged from the deeper histories, ideas, and traditions that have given the region its distinctive character. Within this narrow framing, we become familiar with the region’s wounds without fully understanding the history behind them. Societies cannot be understood solely through their tragedies. They must also be understood through the histories, ideas, institutions, religious traditions, and political struggles that precede those tragedies. This is where Ochonu’s book proves particularly valuable. Ostensibly a study of Boko Haram, the book derives its deeper significance from its insistence that the insurgency cannot be adequately understood as an isolated contemporary phenomenon. Boko Haram emerged from a historical landscape marked by Islamic reform, religious contestation, struggles over authority, political transformation, and competing interpretations of legitimate governance. Such historical depth is often missing from public discourse. Boko Haram has been variously explained through poverty, unemployment, political exclusion, corruption, state failure, climate pressures, religious extremism, and international jihadist networks. Each explanation illuminates part of the problem, but none, standing alone, is sufficient. Ochonu’s contribution is to situate these contemporary realities within a much longer historical continuum while resisting the temptation to treat historical antecedents as inevitable causes. That distinction is crucial. To explain is not to excuse. Understanding the intellectual and historical origins of violence does not diminish the culpability of those who murder civilians, abduct children, or terrorise communities. Condemnation is morally indispensable, but it cannot substitute for explanation. A society that understands only the symptoms of its crises will repeatedly find itself surprised by their recurrence. One of the most compelling dimensions of Ochonu’s analysis is his treatment of the political uses of history. Boko Haram has invoked Usman dan Fodio, the nineteenth-century Islamic reformer whose jihad profoundly altered the political and religious architecture of much of what is now Northern Nigeria. Such invocations matter because history is not merely a record of what happened. It can become a reservoir of legitimacy, identity, grievance, and political aspiration. But invocation does not establish inheritance. The fact that Boko Haram appeals to dan Fodio does not, by itself, establish a direct theological or ideological descent from him. Nor does the history of Islamic reform in Northern Nigeria lead inexorably to contemporary jihadism. The intellectual task is more exacting: to determine what connects these historical moments, what separates them, and how contemporary actors selectively appropriate the past to legitimise present ambitions. Here, the politics of history becomes inseparable from the history of politics. The past is not inert. It is remembered, interpreted, contested, reconstructed, and sometimes weaponised. Ochonu also helps preserve a distinction frequently lost in polemical discussions: religious reform is not synonymous with religious extremism. Similarities in language, symbolism, or doctrine may suggest intellectual affinities, but resemblance alone cannot establish causation or direct descent. This distinction is particularly important in understanding Boko Haram’s hostility toward Western education and aspects of modern political life. Movements that denounce modernity can simultaneously exploit its technologies, communications systems, organisational structures, and political mechanisms. The more illuminating question, therefore, is not simply what Boko Haram rejects, but what it selectively appropriates, how its ideology has evolved, and why particular ideas resonate under specific political and social conditions. This is precisely where history must engage with political economy, state conduct, local grievances, and international influences. Poverty does not automatically produce insurgency. Religious conviction does not inevitably lead to violence. Political exclusion does not mechanically generate radicalization. The challenge is to understand how these forces interact and the circumstances under which they become combustible. Ochonu does not pretend to settle every question, nor should he. A single volume cannot exhaust the theological, historical, political, economic, and sociological dimensions of an insurgency whose roots and consequences span generations and national boundaries. Questions will inevitably remain about the precise relationship between earlier religious traditions and contemporary militancy, the role of state violence and international jihadism, the nature of local grievances, and the experiences of communities caught between insurgents and security forces. But a book need not answer every question to change the quality of the questions we ask. That, ultimately, is Ochonu’s achievement. He restores historical depth to a conversation too often dominated by immediate security concerns. He reminds us that Boko Haram is not merely a security problem, but also an intellectual, historical, political, and cultural phenomenon. For me, however, the significance of the book extends beyond Boko Haram. As someone from southern Nigeria, I consider it a valuable resource for anyone who wishes to understand Northern Nigeria beyond stereotype and political caricature. More importantly, it complicates assumptions about a region too often encountered through the shorthand of violence, religion, and political crisis. It invites readers to engage with the religious traditions, intellectual struggles, political formations, and historical experiences that have shaped a region whose destiny remains inseparable from that of the rest of Nigeria. Ultimately, Boko Haram: The Past of the Present Upheaval reminds us that history is neither a mausoleum of dead events nor a deterministic script for the future. It is a contested inheritance from which contemporary actors draw symbols, identities, grievances, ideas, and claims to legitimacy. For a country perpetually confronted by the consequences of an insufficiently examined past, that is an important lesson. A nation does itself a profound disservice when it buries its history rather than confronts it. History does not disappear because a society chooses not to speak about it. It persists in fractured identities, unresolved grievances, political suspicions, and the enduring consequences of decisions made in the past. I know this not merely as an abstraction, but as a matter of personal experience. I am an Igbo man born during the Nigerian Civil War, a conflict that formally ended decades ago but whose consequences remain woven into the lives of people from my part of Nigeria. For many of us, the war is not a distant episode confined to textbooks and archives. Its effects remain visible in our families and communities, as does the enduring sense that an essential chapter of our national story remains incompletely told. This is one of the deeper lessons of Ochonu’s book. His willingness to excavate the historical foundations of Boko Haram demonstrates what becomes possible when we resist the temptation to treat history as an inconvenience. Nigeria needs that same intellectual courage in confronting its own unresolved past. A nation cannot fully understand its present, much less build a more honest and cohesive future, while suppressing the difficult chapters that helped shape it. We do not heal historical wounds by refusing to name them; we merely allow their consequences to persist. For anyone who wishes to understand Northern Nigeria, its culture, religious traditions, intellectual evolution, political formations, and historical encounters, Moses Ochonu’s book is an indispensable place to begin. Mo has been generous enough to make the book universally available. Read it. Engage with it. Allow it to complicate what you thought you already knew. Osmund Agbo is a medical doctor, author, and the 2026 recipient of the Thabo Mbeki Prize for Scholarship and Public Service

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 读过莫的大部分著作，也听过足够多的他的论点后，我有时会觉得自己已经到达了一个奇特的境界：进食、反刍，再度进食，开始像是一顿连绵不断的餐食。然而，当他把自己强大的历史视角投向一个长期令我着迷的主题，即政治伊斯兰主义时，我发现他的最新著作《博科哈拉姆：当下动荡的往昔》令人爱不释手。我这样说明，并不是要宣称自己持客观立场，而是要交代我评介这部作品所处的语境。无论莫西姆斯还是法鲁克，都不是传统意义上的我的导师。更确切地说，他们是与我对话的人和思想同行者；他们的研究、论辩和异议视角以难以量化，丰富了我的思考。作为一名来自南方的基督徒，我早就注意到，我们这些南方人很容易自以为了解尼日利亚北部，却对塑造该地区复杂演变历程的历史潮流、宗教传统和思想激荡其实所知甚浅。我们对北方的理解往往由那些作为头条闯入全国意识的碎片所中介：博科哈拉姆的叛乱、匪患的灾难、伊斯兰教法的政治、对政治伊斯兰主义的焦虑，以及宗教紧张与流血似乎永无止境的恶性循环。我们主要通过其危机的spectacle认识北方，却仍与那些赋予这一地区独特特征，更深层的历史、观念和传统大体疏离。在这种狭窄的框架中，我们熟悉了该地区的创伤，却未能充分理解其背后的历史。社会不能仅凭悲剧来理解。还必须通过悲剧之前的历史、观念、制度、宗教传统和政治斗争来理解它们。奥乔努的书正是在这一点上显得格外有价值。这本书表面上研究博科哈拉姆，但它更深的意义在于坚持认为：这场叛乱无法被充分理解为一种孤立的当代现象。博科哈拉姆出现于一片充满伊斯兰改革、宗教争辩、权力斗争、政治转型以及对合法治理的各种相互竞争性解读的历史图景之中。公共讨论往往缺少这种历史纵深。博科哈拉姆先后被归因于贫困、失业、政治排斥、腐败、国家失灵、气候压力、宗教极端主义和国际圣战网络。每一种解释都揭示了问题的一部分，但没有任何一种单独来看是充分的。奥乔努的贡献，在于把这些当代现实置于长得多的一段历史连续体中，同时避免把历史先例当作不可避免的起因。这种区分至关重要。解释不等于开脱。理解暴力的思想和历史起源，并不会减轻那些杀害平民、绑架儿童或恐吓社区之人的罪责。道德谴责不可或缺，但它不能取代解释。一个只理解自身危机症状的社会，会一再对危机再次出现感到意外。奥乔努分析中最引人注目的维度之一，是他探讨了历史的政治用途。博科哈拉姆援引了乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥，这位19世纪的伊斯兰改革者，其圣战深刻改变了如今尼日利亚北部大片地区的政治与宗教格局。此类援引之所以重要，是因为历史并非仅仅是已发生之事的记录。它可以成为合法性、认同、不满和政治抱负的储备库。然而，援引并不能证明继承关系。博科哈拉姆诉诸丹·福迪奥，这一事实本身并不能证明两者之间存在直接或神学、意识形态上的谱系联系。尼日利亚北部伊斯兰改革的历史，也不会不可避免地导向当代圣战主义。思想任务要求更高：必须确定这些历史时刻之间有何联系、有何区别，以及当代行动者如何有选择地挪用过去，以使当下的抱负获得正当性。在这里，历史的政治与政治的历史变得不可分割。过去并非惰性不变。它会被记忆、解释、争议、重构，有时还会被武器化。奥乔努还帮助保留了辩论中经常被混淆的一项区别：宗教改革并不等同于宗教极端主义。语言、象征或教义上的相似性可能提示思想上的亲缘关系，但仅凭相似之处无法确立因果关系或直接谱系。在理解博科哈拉姆对西方教育和现代政治生活某些方面的敌意时，这一区分尤为重要。谴责现代性的运动，同时也可以利用现代性的技术、通信系统、组织结构和政治机制。因此，更具启发性的问题不只是博科哈拉姆拒绝什么，而是它有选择地挪用了什么，其意识形态如何演变，以及为什么某些观念会在特定政治和社会条件下引起共鸣。历史正是在这里必须同政治经济学、国家行为、地方不满和国际影响展开对话。贫困不会自动催生叛乱。宗教信仰不会必然导致暴力。政治排斥不会机械地产生激进化。真正的挑战是理解这些力量如何相互作用，以及在何种情况下它们会变得易燃。奥乔努并未假装能够解决每一个问题，他也不应当如此。一卷书不可能穷尽一场叛乱的全部神学、历史、政治、经济和社会学维度；这场叛乱的根源和后果跨越数代人与国界。关于早期宗教传统与当代武装活动之间的确切关系、国家暴力和国际圣战主义所起的作用、地方不满的性质，以及夹在叛乱分子与安全部队之间的社区所经历的一切，问题无疑仍将存在。但一本书不必回答所有问题，也能改变我们提出问题的质量。归根结底，这正是奥乔努的成就。他把历史纵深还原给一场往往被眼前安全考虑主导的讨论。他提醒我们，博科哈拉姆不仅是一个安全问题，也是一种思想、历史、政治和文化现象。然而，对我而言，这本书的意义超出了博科哈拉姆本身。作为一名来自尼日利亚南部的人，我认为，对于任何希望超越刻板印象和政治漫画化认识尼日利亚北部的人而言，它都是一部宝贵的资源。更重要的是，它使人们对这个常常只通过暴力、宗教和政治危机等简略标签来认识的地区的种种假设变得更加复杂。它邀请读者深入接触那些塑造了一个地区的宗教传统、思想斗争、政治形态和历史经历，而这个地区的命运至今仍与尼日利亚其他地区密不可分Ultimately，《博科哈拉姆：当下动荡的往昔》提醒我们，历史既不是死寂事件的陵墓，也不是决定未来的宿命脚本。它是一份有争议的遗产，当代行动者从中汲取符号、身份、不满、观念和正当性主张。对一个永远面对过去遭充分审视所遗留后果的国家来说，这是一堂重要的课。一个国家若掩埋自己的历史，而不是正视它，就是在严重地伤害自身。社会不会因为选择不谈论历史，历史便消失。它会继续存在于支离破碎的身份中、未解决的不满中、政治猜疑中，以及过去所作决定的长久后果之中。我知道这一点，不只是把它当作抽象概念，而是作为切身体验。我是一名伊博人，出生于尼日利亚内战期间；这场冲突在数十年前正式结束，但其后果至今仍编织在来自我所在地区 peoples 的生活之中。对我们许多人来说，战争并非只存在于教科书和档案中的遥远往事。它在我们家庭和社区中留下的影响依然可见，那种认为国家叙事中一个关键章节仍未被完整讲述的 enduring 感觉也依然存在。这是奥乔努之书更深层的教训之一。他愿意发掘博科哈拉姆的历史基础，展示了当我们抵制把历史视为麻烦的诱惑时，能够实现什么。尼日利亚在面对自身尚未解决的过去时，也需要同样的思想勇气。一个国家若压制塑造自己的艰难篇章，就不可能充分理解自己的现在，更谈不上建设更诚实、更凝聚的未来。拒绝说出历史创伤，并不能疗愈它们；我们只是任其后果延续下去。对于任何希望了解尼日利亚北部、其文化、宗教传统、思想演变、政治形态和历史际遇的人而言，莫西姆斯·奥乔努的书都是不可或缺的起点。莫已慷慨地让这本书向所有人开放。请读它。与它对话。让它使你以为自己早已了解的事情变得复杂。奥斯蒙德·阿博是一名医学博士、作家，也是2026年塔博·姆贝基学术与公共服务奖得主

https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.summary: Teodoro was responding to a report by a Manila-based Chinese language newspaper that China was considering removing the warship from Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal as one of 10 possible “countermeasures” against the Philippines following increasingly strained bilateral ties over the maritime conflict between the two countries.
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.summary_zh: 特奥多罗是在回应马尼拉一家中文报纸的报道。该报称，在两国围绕海上冲突的双边关系日益紧张之际，中国正考虑将军舰撤出阿永金（第二托马斯）浅滩，作为针对菲律宾的10项可能“反制措施”之一。
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.body: Teodoro was responding to a report by a Manila-based Chinese language newspaper that China was considering removing the warship from Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal as one of 10 possible “countermeasures” against the Philippines following increasingly strained bilateral ties over the maritime conflict between the two countries. “Any threat against BRP Sierra Madre will be taken very seriously because it will be an act against a military vessel of the Republic of the Philippines,” Teodoro said in an online interview with reporters. READ: Teodoro: China’s attempt to tow BRP Sierra Madre by force an act of war The ship, now rusted and decrepit, was intentionally run aground at Ayungin to serve as a military outpost in the West Philippine Sea in 1999, four years after China occupied Panganiban (Mischief) Reef, which, like Ayungin, is within the exclusive economic zone of the Philippines. Another reported countermeasure was to halt the resupply of the troops on the Sierra Madre, who rely on fuel, food, water, medicines and other resources delivered by sea. It added that if the Philippines “forcibly breaks through Chinese blockades, China will take strong measures to block them.” The 10 measures were outlined in a report on Friday by the Chinese Commercial News, which noted that there was no official confirmation that these “potential options” were being considered or had been approved by Beijing. It quoted “well-informed sources” saying that the “Chinese side” was “gradually losing patience with recent Philippine actions and related statements concerning China,” a reference to strident exchanges between Philippine officials and Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan and his embassy related to the maritime dispute between the two countries. The possible countermeasures include banning “anti-China” Filipino politicians and their immediate families from entering any Chinese territory, freezing their assets in China and prohibiting Chinese entities from conducting business with them; and publicly disclosing their commercial and financial dealings with China. The others are restricting Chinese citizens from traveling to the Philippines; tightening labor policies on Filipino workers in Hong Kong and Macao; arresting more Filipinos illegally working in China; closing certain consulates in China, including in Hong Kong, if Manila approves the establishment of an additional Taiwan office in Cebu. The proposed economic sanctions include cutting off fuel and fertilizer supply and restricting exports of urgently needed and essential goods to the Philippines. “It’s not a state of war … but an act of war because it is an offensive act against a Philippine warship,” he said. Only the President and Congress could declare a state of war, he said. Under the Constitution, Congress has the power to declare the existence of a state of war by a two-thirds vote of both houses in joint session, voting separately. Asked whether an attempt by China to board the Sierra Madre could trigger the Philippines’ Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) with the United States, Teodoro said the possibility remained open, although the decision would ultimately rest with President Marcos. He emphasized that such an incident could, rather than necessarily would, lead to the invocation of the 1951 treaty, which commits the Philippines and the United States to act in accordance with their respective constitutional processes to respond to an armed attack against either party in the Pacific. Several US officials, including secretaries of state and defense, and American diplomats have said that Washington would stand by its “ironclad” commitments under the treaty. Washington has affirmed that the treaty covers armed attacks against Philippine armed forces, public vessels and aircraft, including those of the Philippine Coast Guard, anywhere in the South China Sea. Asked to comment on the two proposed economic sanctions, Teodoro said the country’s dependence on China could be used against it. “It just goes to show you that whatever supposed goodwill that they are doing is a weapon and they are weaponizing it,” he said. Teodoro urged the government and private sector to strengthen domestic industries and diversify supply chains, particularly for critical infrastructure. “We cannot place complete trust in a country that claims our territory,” he said. Teodoro said the Philippines needed to reduce its dependence on Chinese products and suppliers, warning that economic relationships could be used as leverage during disputes over sovereignty and territorial rights. The defense chief also urged companies to diversify their sources of raw materials and finished products instead of relying heavily on a single country. “We are constantly being threatened subtly and now more overtly,” he said. Amid the continuing tensions, Teodoro renewed his call to overhaul the country’s military modernization law, warning that the existing framework was hampering efforts to secure sufficient funding for the Armed Forces of the Philippines. The defense establishment had been “stuck” to receiving the relatively small P50 billion allocation for military upgrades because of the modernization law, Teodoro said. He said the current spending system was “restrictive and no longer suited to present realities.” Teodoro called for a stronger domestic defense industry, saying the Philippines needed to develop basic industries that could support the local production of military equipment, citing South Korea and India as examples. The recent angry exchanges between Filipino officials and Chinese diplomats followed Jing’s remarks on Oct. 15. He was responding to reporters’ questions about a statement by Teodoro who said that China was the “lone troublemaker” in Southeast Asia. Jing said this was “nonsense” as the region was peaceful and that it was fortunate to have a neighbor like China. Jing added, however, that China “may easily win” against the Philippines but chose not to use force because it was peace-loving. The President regarded what he said as a threat and an undiplomatic statement. On Monday, Foreign Secretary Teresa Lazaro summoned Jing to protest against his remarks. Some Philippine lawmakers saw Jing’s remarks as a threat and several sought to declare him as persona non grata and to have him expelled. The Chinese embassy retaliated in a series of social media posts, saying that Filipino politicians with personal political ambitions were undermining Philippine-China relations. https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.title_zh: 吉博·特奥多罗：若中国试图拖走Sierra Madre，就等于“宣战”
https://www.inquirer.net/493760/gibo-teo.body_zh: Teodoro是在回应马尼拉一家中文报纸的报道。该报称，在两国围绕海上冲突的双边关系日益紧张之际，中国正考虑将军舰撤出Ayungin（Second Thomas）浅滩，并将其列为针对菲律宾的10项可能“反制措施”之一。Teodoro在线接受记者采访时说：“任何针对BRP Sierra Madre的威胁都会受到极为严肃的对待，因为这将构成针对菲律宾共和国军舰的行为。”阅读：Teodoro：中国试图强行拖走BRP Sierra Madre属于战争行为。这艘如今已经锈蚀破败的军舰于1999年被故意搁浅在Ayungin，作为菲律宾西海的一个军事前哨。那是在中国占领Panganiban（Mischief）礁4年后；Panganiban与Ayungin一样，均位于菲律宾专属经济区内。另一项被报道的反制措施是停止向Sierra Madre上的部队补给。这些部队依赖海运获得燃料、食物、饮用水、药品和其他物资。报道还称，如果菲律宾“强行突破中国的封锁，中国将采取有力措施予以阻止”。这10项措施是中国商业新闻周五发布的一份报告所列。报告指出，没有官方消息证实这些“潜在选项”正在考虑之中或已获北京批准。报告援引“消息灵通人士”的话说，中方“正逐渐失去对菲律宾近期涉华行动及相关言论的耐心”，这是指菲律宾官员与中国大使景泉及其使馆就两国海上争端进行的激烈交锋。可能采取的反制措施包括：禁止“反华”的菲律宾政治人物及其直系亲属进入任何中国领土，冻结他们在中国的资产，禁止中国实体与其开展业务，并公开披露他们与中国的商业和金融往来。其他措施包括限制中国公民赴菲律宾旅行；收紧针对在香港和澳门工作的菲律宾人的劳工政策；逮捕更多在中国非法工作的菲律宾人；如果马尼拉批准在宿务增设台湾办事处，就关闭中国境内的某些领事馆，包括香港的领事馆。建议实施的经济制裁包括切断对菲律宾的燃料和化肥供应，并限制向菲律宾出口急需品和基本物资。他说：“这不是战争状态……但属于战争行为，因为这是针对菲律宾军舰的进攻性行为。”他说，只有总统和国会才能宣布进入战争状态。根据《宪法》，国会可在两院联席会议中分别表决，以三分之二多数决定是否进入战争状态。被问及中国试图登上Sierra Madre是否会触发菲律宾与美国签订的《共同防御条约》（MDT）时，Teodoro表示这种可能性仍然存在，尽管最终决定权将掌握在Marcos总统手中。他强调，此类事件可能、但不一定必然导致援引1951年条约。该条约承诺，菲律宾和美国将依照各自宪法程序，共同应对任何一方在太平洋地区遭受的武装攻击。包括国务卿、国防部长在内的多名美国官员以及美国外交官都表示，华盛顿将恪守条约规定的“铁定”承诺。华盛顿确认，该条约涵盖针对菲律宾武装部队、公共船舶和飞机的武装攻击，包括菲律宾海岸警卫队任何位于南海的船舶和飞机。被要求评论拟议中的两项经济制裁时，Teodoro说，该国对中国的依赖可能被用来对付菲律宾。他说：“这恰恰说明，无论他们所谓的善意是什么，那都是一种武器，而且他们正把这种善意武器化。”Teodoro敦促政府和私营部门加强国内产业并推动供应链多元化，尤其是关键基础设施领域。他说：“我们不能完全信任一个声称觊觎我们领土的国家。”Teodoro表示，菲律宾需要减少对中国产品和供应商的依赖，并警告称，在主权和领土权利争端中，经济关系可能被用作施压杠杆。这名国防部长还敦促企业多元化采购原材料和制成品的来源，而不是严重依赖单一国家。他说：“我们不断受到隐性威胁，如今还面临更加公开的威胁。”在紧张局势持续之际，Teodoro再次呼吁全面改革该国的军事现代化法，并警告称，现有框架妨碍了为菲律宾武装部队争取充足资金。Teodoro说，受现代化法限制，国防体系一直“受困于”只能获得相对较小的500亿比索军备升级拨款。他说，现行支出制度“限制性太强，已不再符合当前现实”。Teodoro呼吁建立更强大的国内国防工业，称菲律宾需要发展能够支持本地生产军事装备的基础工业，并列举韩国和印度为例。菲律宾官员与中国外交官近期激烈交锋，源于景泉10月15日发表的言论。当时记者就Teodoro关于中国是东南亚“唯一麻烦制造者”的说法向他提问。景泉称这种说法“荒谬”，因为该地区是和平的，而能有中国这样的邻国是幸运的。不过，景泉补充说，中国“很容易战胜”菲律宾，但选择不使用武力，因为中国热爱和平。总统认为他的言论是一种威胁，也是不符合外交礼节的言论。周一，外交部长Teresa Lazaro召见景泉，就其言论提出抗议。一些菲律宾议员将景泉的言论视为威胁，数名议员试图宣布其为不受欢迎人物并将其驱逐。中国使馆在一系列社交媒体帖子中反击称，怀有个人政治野心的菲律宾政治人物正在破坏菲中关系。无法保存您的订阅。请重试。您的订阅已成功。该使馆向议员发出挑战，要求他们“停止虚张声势”，宣布景泉为不受欢迎人物。中国使馆说：“就这么做。”INQ https://leadership.ng/msmes-analysts-say.summary_zh: 尼日利亚小微企业主协会（ASBON）主席Femi Egbesola博士表示，降息尚未转化为中小微型企业（MSMEs）能够负担且便捷获得的信贷。他说：“许多中小微企业的现实情况是，尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）的降息尚未转化为价格可负担、获取便捷的信贷。
https://leadership.ng/msmes-analysts-say.body: The president of the Association of Small Business Owners of Nigeria (ASBON), Dr. Femi Egbesola, said the rate cut had not yet translated into affordable and accessible credit for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). He described the fall in private sector credit as a worrying signal. “The reality for many MSMEs is that the CBN’s rate cut has not yet translated into affordable, accessible credit. This is a worrying signal, although the aggregate figures alone do not explain why lending declined,” he said. He said small businesses still face high borrowing costs, stringent collateral requirements and short repayment periods that make bank loans inaccessible. “For small businesses, high borrowing costs, stringent collateral requirements and short repayment periods remain major barriers. Banks must also consider credit risks, but viable businesses should not be excluded simply because they lack landed property or other conventional collateral,” he said. According to him, the credit squeeze is crippling MSMEs’ ability to operate and expand. “The credit squeeze means businesses struggle to purchase raw materials, maintain production, invest in equipment and employ more workers,” Egbesola noted. He said fintechs are filling the gap with quick loans, but their model is not suitable for long-term industrial growth. “Fintech loans offer speed and convenience, but their short tenures and potentially high costs may not be suitable for financing factories or long-term expansion,” he said. Egbesola urged the CBN to go beyond rate cuts and adopt structural measures. “I urge the CBN to strengthen credit-guarantee schemes, expand cash-flow-based lending and movable-asset financing, and introduce measurable targets and incentives for bank lending to viable MSMEs,” he said. He also called for transparency in bank lending to small businesses. “Banks should be required to report transparently on their MSME lending performance, with appropriate regulatory consequences for persistent non-compliance. The objective is not to compel reckless lending, but to make productive businesses bankable and ensure that monetary easing translates into investment, jobs and economic growth,” Egbesola added. The chief operating officer of InvestData Consulting Limited, Mr. Ambrose Omordion, said banks appear not to be aligned with the CBN’s strategy of making funds cheaper to boost Gross Domestic Product. “Anywhere in the world, banks are the engine of any economy. Nigerian banks are sitting on liquid funds that should be lent to the public, but they are yet to understand how to do that lending because they have not been doing enough lending as before,” Omordion said. He said fintech banks have taken over the retail lending space, offering quick loans without demanding high collateral, a model traditional banks are struggling to replicate. Omordion said many deposit money banks prefer investing in risk-free treasury bills and remain cautious because of past experience with high non-performing loans, especially from exposure to the oil and gas and telecommunications sectors. “The CBN cut rates to boost the economy and push banks to lend to the real sector, but banks are dragging their feet in implementing the rate cut. The CBN has the hammer and can sanction any bank that defaults,” he said. He said increased lending would drive GDP growth, as no government can drive growth alone without the private sector. “Banks have the money and can drive new sectors. We want lending to expand so that industries and enterprises can produce more when they have access to cheaper funds,” he said. Omordion added that the entry of foreign banks, such as J.P. Morgan setting up a merchant bank in Nigeria, shows the potential in the economy and should push local banks to develop better lending strategies. Data from the CBN show that private sector credit dropped to N83.93 trillion in September from N84.47 trillion in August, a decline of 0.64 per cent. The figure is still about 15.7 per cent higher than the N72.53 trillion recorded a year earlier. The decline followed the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in September to cut the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) by 350 basis points to 23 per cent, the largest reduction in the benchmark rate since December 2006. The MPC retained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for commercial banks at 45 per cent. The CBN data do not explain whether the fall reflects weaker loan demand, tighter lending conditions, repayments or other factors. A lower benchmark rate can also take time to filter through, as actual lending depends on banks’ funding costs, risk assessments and borrowers’ ability to repay. We’ve got the edge.
